main_text.l: Sermo frequens de te, & DOUSAEO multum
in ore
EMMIUS: Historiae hoc visa merere Fides;
Incorrupta Fides. quæ quo per tempora nostra
Rarior, hoc pluris est faciunda mihi,
Cattigenisq; meis: res quorum ex ordine
ge-stas
Te sparsim Frisiis inseruisse tuis,
Et video, & lætor. quo nullum, hoc scilicet
ævo, In genere hoc Belgis clarius extat opus.
Vera, nec intestata loquor. scit Grotius istud,
Doctrinâ verè Magnus & ingenio:
Et norunt alij plures, quid maxima gentis
Gloria Gallorum sentiat EMMERIUS;
EMMERIUS, de te solitus qui plurima amicè
Quærere, & in laudes luxuriare tuas:
Ante alia Annales merito admirarier unos,
Expensos Frisiis quos tulit UBBO suis.
Ter quater ô felix antiqui temporis ætas,
Cui facundo adeò contigit ore cani!
Vos quoque fœlices tanto scriptore Libelli;
Ingenij rari, nec minus artis opus:
Vos ego sæpè meo vos Elogio ornaturus,
Testabor veterum laudibus esse pares.
HIRCI-

page.notes: The title line and the first lines are set in italic type, as printed. The large S of "Sermo" is joined to its word. "Cattigenisq;" is set in small capitals, as printed. The closing "HIRCI-" is read as the letter's signature (a name abbreviated or cut off at the hyphen); it is not a catchword, since it stands at the end of the text and carries a hyphen. It is set right-aligned in the original, which cannot be shown here. The pointing mark before "Doctrinâ" and the faint mark at the bottom are not printed text and are left out. The Google digitisation watermark at the bottom right is left out. No page number is printed.
